proof:
The base hull is the unit crosspolytope, whose only integer points are its vertices and zero. Outer bases are exposed, and all guard fibers are contained in $T$, so the central fiber stays exactly $T$. The hull spans the full ambient space. A guard's area is $v$ and its own covariance about its own centroid is $\sigma^2\Sigma_T$. Summing the volume-weighted centered covariance tensors and dividing by $V+6Lv$ gives the displayed covariance factor.

For a continuous direction $u\ne0$, choose $i$ maximizing $u\cdot v_i=A>0$. The three vertex values sum to zero, so all are at least $-2A$. Hence $u\cdot x\ge(1-3\sigma)A>0$ throughout $D_i$. At corresponding points of the two copies at $\pm e_{i,r}$, the two through-origin margins sum to $2u\cdot x>0$ for any base tilt. At least one ramp is one; the other is nonnegative. Integrate on each of the $L$ pairs to get outside mass at least $Lv$ for every direction and tilt.

For $u=\nabla\lambda_i$ the central margin is $\lambda_i-1/3$. Set the matching tilt coefficients to $1$ and all others to zero. The positive matching guards are fully captured and the negative ones missed strictly beyond the ramp, since $-1+\lambda_i-1/3\le-1/3$. Nonmatching guards satisfy $\lambda_i\le\sigma$ so their margins are at most $-1/12<-w$. Thus the outside lower bound is attained with strict saturation. By w31-triangle-outward-own-minimum the own lower bound is $V(4/9+2w/3+w^2/3)$, with equality precisely in those three directions. Pure-base caps through zero retain $T$ and at least one guard on every reflected axis, hence have mass at least $V+3Lv>Q$. This proves the asserted exact depth at the origin.

At any other point of the central triangle, at least one canonical normal has strictly positive projection on the mark displacement because those normals span and sum to zero. Raising that cap's threshold strictly loses own mass at first, since its open ramp crosses the interior of $T$; monotonicity preserves a strict loss for larger shifts. On an exposed outer base a pure-base cap isolates its own mass $v<Q$. Thus the origin uniquely maximizes depth.

For any active cap, both the own and outside lower bounds must be attained. Its continuous direction is consequently canonical $i$. Each of the $L$ matching pairs has cost at least $v$, so each costs exactly $v$ and every nonmatching guard costs zero. In a matching pair at least one ramp is pointwise one. If either ramp had a value in $(0,1)$ anywhere on its guard, continuity and density of the interior would give positive area on which the pair pays strictly more than one. Thus both ramps are saturated on the entire closed guard. Connectedness makes each constant; exactly one of the pair is one. The zero costs similarly imply the other guards' ramps are identically zero. Only the own triangle contributes threshold coarea. In the displayed barycentric normalization these coareas are equal and positive, since affine permutations of the vertices preserve area and all three widths agree. Coarea times normal is invariant under positive rescaling of the normal. The unique positive relation among the three spanning continuous normals has equal coefficients, hence any balanced response menu assigns total weight $1/3$ to each class. Only one class can pay on any guard, yielding the pointwise bound.
statement:
Let $L\ge1$ be an integer, $T$ any nondegenerate centroid-zero triangle of area $V$ with vertices $v_i$, and $0<\sigma\le1/4$. Put $D_i=(1-\sigma)v_i+\sigma T$ and $v=\sigma^2V$. Take the convex hull of $\{0\}\times T$ and the lifted copies of $D_i$ at all reflected independent axes $\pm e_{i,r}$ in $\mathbb R^{3L}$, $1\le r\le L$. Its actual integer fibers are exactly these prescribed fibers. Its mass is $M=V+6Lv$ and its pooled within-fiber covariance is $\kappa_L\Sigma_T$ with $\kappa_L=(1+6L\sigma^4)/(1+6L\sigma^2)$.

For fixed $h>0$ use the actual covariance norm for the uniform outward smoothing width; a cap of affine margin $m$ and continuous normal $u$ has profile $\Psi(m/(h\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\kappa_L\Sigma_Tu}))$ with $\Psi(s)=\min(1,\max(0,1+s))$. Pure-base caps remain ordinary closed caps. If $0<w=h\sqrt{\kappa_L/18}\le1/100$, the unique deepest mark is $(0,0)$, with raw depth $Q=V(4/9+2w/3+w^2/3)+Lv$. Every active cap is canonical in some direction $\nabla\lambda_i$, captures exactly one whole guard from each matching pair $\pm e_{i,r}$ and misses every nonmatching guard, with zero outside transition coarea. Every balanced active response menu gives total probability weight $1/3$ to each direction. Here balance means the probability-weighted mean of the continuous normals times their raw threshold coareas is zero. In particular every menu profile is at most $1/3$ pointwise on each guard boundary.
title: Independent reflected triangle guards have an exact all-active menu
